original_test_intent: Verify that customer BMC firmware no longer exposes AMD GPU debug forwarding on TCP ports 50080 and 50443.
original_method: Confirm the exact customer build, inspect the correct BMC/DUT network namespaces for listeners or forwarding, and run bounded probes to both ports from every approved reachability vantage without changing services or policy.
manual_activity: Provide the exact customer-build manifest, ownership of the BMC and DUT network namespaces, authorized local/external probe vantage points and the accepted interpretation of refusal, timeout/filtering and protocol response for both ports.
required_inputs: BMC versus DUT network namespace map
Authorized target addresses and vantage points
safety_requirements: Do not use sshpass or disable host-key checking
Do not start a debug service
Do not add, remove or flush firewall/NAT/forwarding rules
Do not treat timeout as proof of service removal
Stop and report any exposure without remediation
agent_execution_scope: Capture read-only listener and forwarding baselines
Classify connection, refusal, timeout and protocol response separately
engineer_actions: Provide build, target and vantage inventory
Resolve source's omitted 50443 procedure by requiring title-level dual-port coverage

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its `ss` inspection covers both numbers but may run in the wrong DUT namespace, while localhost curl covers only 50080; sshpass and host-key bypass are unsafe and neither command proves external BMC exposure is absent.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: On each approved target namespace, inspect listeners/forwarding read-only and perform bounded TCP probes to both ports from each approved local and external vantage, recording connection/refusal/timeout/protocol evidence separately.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both specified ports, GPU-equipped system context and 15/10 timing remain; build identity, target namespaces, addresses and vantage policy are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Combine target-side listener/forwarding evidence with independent both-port connection probes so absence of a local process is not confused with absence of remotely reachable forwarding.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes plaintext credentials, covers omitted 50443, restores the BMC-facing perspective and distinguishes service removal from filtering rather than printing an expected-no-output marker.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Verifies exposure only on the approved interfaces and vantage points; it does not establish absence on untested VLANs, IPv6, alternate namespaces or customer deployments not represented by the bound build.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A firewall timeout can conceal a listener, and a listener in a BMC namespace may be invisible from the host OS. Negative evidence is valid only for the enumerated paths.

project_override_considerations: If customer policy requires ports to be absent rather than merely externally blocked, target-side listener/forwarding evidence is mandatory. If filtering is an accepted control, record that as a separate policy outcome and do not call it removal.
expected_evidence: Exact customer BMC/DUT build and GPU platform identity
Per-target listener/forwarding results for both ports
Per-vantage bounded TCP results for 50080 and 50443

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items requires removal of both 50080 and 50443, but Procedure issues a connection only to 50080 and Criteria describes one command. The review preserves the dual-port title as required scope and records that the original Procedure cannot by itself cover 50443.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Customer-build identity, namespace/vantage inventory and negative-test semantics are identifiable package inputs; the omitted second probe can be added in the review without guessing a dangerous operation, so the case is REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Turns an incomplete credential-leaking single-port request into a dual-port, multi-vantage security negative test that distinguishes removal from filtering and preserves the source's unresolved coverage mismatch.
independent_technical_reasoning: A host-side `ss` result cannot prove that a BMC-resident forwarding service is absent, and a BMC-side listener alone cannot prove external reachability. Both target inspection and independent probes are needed. The test names two ports but executes only 50080, so 50443 coverage cannot be inferred from one failure. A TCP timeout is also weaker than refusal because an intermediate filter may hide exposure; any established connection or HTTP/TLS response, even an error, proves a reachable endpoint. No remediation is authorized by this verification case.
